items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Around that time, Tommy Dorsey had this arrangement on 'The Song Of India' that was very popular.

ctx.x: Around that time, Tommy Dorsey had this arrangement on "The Song Of India" that was very popular. And I think this was my first association with arranging. In this group, we had four pieces. We had piano, drums, trumpet, and of course, the saxophone player who played clarinet too. He and I sat down, and I gave him the notes to play on his clarinet. Then the trumpet player, we'd tell him certain notes to play, and we'd wind up playing something separately that sounded like Tommy Dorsey, which was a big hit in the…

So we came back to Washington, and I think this would be 1936, somewhere around there... When you think back, you kind of forget exactly where they are chronologically, but it's around in the same time. But chronologically, one thing might have happened before the other.
